Given the checkpoints, the simplest fix is to reset AutoStep to 0 when Mode changes from FALSE to TRUE (rising edge), or when returning to auto mode, reinitialize based on current sensors. But is that supported by public requirements? Mode switching to auto should start automatic control; it likely should re-evaluate sensors. However it doesn't explicitly say. But the test clearly expects that after manual, when SensorFeed is true, the motor starts. So we need to make the auto state reinitialize when Mode becomes true after being false. Or perhaps we should not preserve AutoStep across mode changes. We can add a rising edge detector for Mode: when Mode transitions from false to true, set AutoStep based on current sensors (like the initial AutoInit but perhaps without AutoInit). So the fix is to reinitialize auto state when Mode transitions from false to true, i.e., add a rising edge detector on Mode and if it rises, set AutoStep based on current sensors (like initialization). But we already have AutoInit only on first scan; we should extend to also trigger when Mode goes from false to true (not first scan). If Mode rises later, we run init again, possibly overwriting state. That is okay because mode just switched to auto.

We also need to ensure that the manual branch does not interfere. Currently, after AutoInit block, then IF NOT Mode THEN manual and RETURN. So if Mode is false, we never run auto initialization. That's fine. For rising edge, we need to detect within the scan when Mode is true and previous Mode was false. We can add an R_TRIG for Mode in VAR. Then in the initialization section, after AutoInit false check (first scan), add another condition: IF ModeRise.Q THEN set AutoStep based on sensors, but only when Mode is true? The R_TRIG will be true on the first scan that Mode is true after being false. So we can include it in the IF init block. But we must avoid double initialization on the first scan when Mode might be true: if first scan Mode true, AutoInit false triggers init; ModeRise.Q might also be true because previous CLK for R_TRIG is false? In CODESYS, R_TRIG's Q is true on first call if CLK true? Typically R_TRIG initializes M to FALSE, so if CLK true on first call, Q true. That could cause double init but not harmful if we ensure the init block is executed once per condition and we combine with OR. We can restructure:

VAR
    rtMode : R_TRIG;
    ModeRise : BOOL;
END_VAR

Then before init logic:
rtMode(CLK := Mode);
ModeRise := rtMode.Q;

Then condition:

    AutoInit := TRUE;  // maybe set true if first
    // reinitialize AutoStep based on sensors

    ELSIF SensorFiring THEN AutoStep := 60;
    ELSIF SensorWeight THEN AutoStep := 40;
    ELSIF SensorWash THEN AutoStep := 20;
    ELSIF SensorFeed THEN AutoStep := 10;
    ELSE AutoStep := 0;
    END_IF;
END_IF;

But note: ModeRise will be true for the first scan if Mode true. That's okay because AutoInit false also true, so it will run once. But we need to ensure that if Mode is false (manual), we don't trigger reinit because we should not alter auto state while in manual? Actually we may not want to reinit when Mode false (the rising edge isn't present because false). So that's fine.

But there is a subtlety: The reinitialization happens before the manual branch, so on the scan where Mode rises to true, we set AutoStep, then continue through auto logic. That is correct.
